description: The bar chart illustrates the “effect” of different probing methods on various language families, as evaluated in the context of multilingual BERT models, likely measuring how well the models capture morphosyntactic features. The horizontal axis lists language families: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic, IE-other, Semitic, and Uralic. The vertical axis, labeled “effect,” ranges from 0 to 40, with tick marks at intervals of 10, and represents a quantitative metric (likely a probing score or effect size) with error bars indicating variability or confidence intervals. Four methods are compared, distinguished by color and labeled in the legend: mBERT-targ (light blue), XLM-targ (dark blue), mBERT-permute (light green), and XLM-permute (dark green). For most language families, mBERT-targ and XLM-targ show higher effect values than their permute counterparts, suggesting that targeted probing outperforms permuted (likely baseline or control) probing. Notably, in IE-other and Uralic, mBERT-targ achieves the highest effect (around 35 and 29, respectively), while in IE-Indic, mBERT-permute and XLM-permute reach relatively high values (~18). The Semitic and Uralic families show the lowest overall effects, especially for permute methods, with some values near zero. Error bars vary in length, indicating differing levels of uncertainty across conditions, with some bars (e.g., IE-Indic mBERT-permute) having notably large error bars. The chart does not sort categories by effect size, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond color coding.
